clue.text: Enquiry among the management, but the query is not reported

indicators.note: the enquiry sits among the letters of the management word, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: the direction of a firm is its management, the people who run it
a quest is a search or enquiry

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question of a company's bosses, but it goes unrecorded.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar a question is either put straight or reported in indirect speech; the definition describes the first kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A question put in the speaker's own words, as opposed to indirect reported speech, is called this in grammar.

clue.text: Strange land he and I took in

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the following words come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes taking in a strange land with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange land' reads like a foreign country, but 'Strange' is the scrambling signal; the I stays at the front, and 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to breathe something in, so took in is a synonym in the breathing sense.

clue.text: Good boy caught with a coin in his grasp — how odd!

indicators.note: the boy holds the other pieces, so they go inside his name

parts.note: Eric, the hero of the Victorian moral tale Eric, or Little by Little, is the crossword's stock good boy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A well-behaved lad is caught clutching money, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good boy' as ERIC is an old crossword convention from a Victorian school story; 'how' only introduces the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person or thing is peculiar, so the adjective is a straight synonym.

clue.text: One who counts or recounts

explanation.surface: A person who tallies figures, or tells stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank clerk counting cash or a vote counter has this title, and so does a storyteller relating events.

clue.text: Release a faun injured by a gun

indicators.note: an injured creature is bent out of shape, so the letters of faun are rearranged

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A woodland creature hurt by gunfire is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges FAUN to UNFA; 'by' sets STEN beside it. The first 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to undo or free, so release is a synonym.

clue.text: Writing up about fighting in a crowd

indicators.note: the reversed writing goes around the fighting, enclosing it
in a down clue going up means the letters for writing are read bottom to top

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
war is fighting between nations

explanation.surface: Someone writes up a report on a brawl in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MS into SM in this down clue; 'in a' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to throng or press together in great numbers, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Succeed in it. without a woman

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the words in it surround the woman

parts.note: the two words are taken as written
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone thrives in a situation without any female help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, an old sense crosswords keep alive. The full stop after 'it' is OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to come into a title or estate on someone's death, which is to succeed to it.

clue.text: Its neighbour had a hundred for north

definitions.text: Its neighbour had a hundred for north

indicators.note: the hundred stands where north now stands, one piece replacing the other

parts.note: the former English county of Cumberland bordered this one to the west
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the word north taken as written

explanation.surface: A county's neighbour once had a hundred where it now has north.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumberland and Northumberland were neighbouring counties in northern England. Replace the C (100) of CUMBERLAND with NORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue identifies the north-east English county by comparison with its western neighbour.

clue.text: Note which makes one tremble after death on the motorway

indicators.note: the trembling piece follows the death and motorway pieces in the answer

parts.note: demise is a formal word for death
M stands for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one
to quaver is to shake or tremble

explanation.surface: A frightening musical note is linked to a fatal crash on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: M for motorway is a British road label (the M1, M25).
explanation.definitionFit: A demisemiquaver is a thirty-second note in music, so it is a kind of musical note.

clue.text: I go into a mixed chalet but it is not immoral

indicators.note: the I is placed inside the scrambled letters
mixed means the letters of chalet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone enters a mixed-sex chalet but insists nothing improper happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges CHALET to ETHCAL and 'go into' puts I inside: ETH-I-CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct is morally right, so it is the opposite of wicked behaviour.

clue.text: Bird covering exploit with girl

parts.note: a feat is a notable deed or exploit
her stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A girl covers up some bold exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage on a bird is made of these, so it is what covers a bird's body.

clue.text: Is about to speak maliciously for people like us

indicators.note: the letters of is go around the malicious speech

parts.note: to slander is to speak falsely and maliciously of someone

explanation.surface: Someone is about to gossip spitefully about the British.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes for readers in Britain, an island nation, so 'people like us' are island dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of an island nation such as Britain are inhabitants of an island.

clue.text: Town parade

explanation.surface: A town holds a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: March is a market town in Cambridgeshire, England; to march is also to parade in step.

clue.text: Ancestral trees?

parts.note: a family tree suggests forebears, but these are both the older generation and small shrubs bearing berries

explanation.surface: A family tree of one's forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders are senior members of a family or community, and also shrubs of the genus Sambucus.

clue.text: One appears twice in the turbulent stream, one after the other

indicators.note: turbulent water churns, so the letters are mixed up
the single letter for one is written down two times

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a single figure twice in rough water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears twice' gives II, and 'turbulent' rearranges it with STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim is Latin for point by point in order, that is in sequence.

clue.text: Rigid but nice tails are twisted

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of nice tails are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Something stiff, though its pretty tails are bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges NICE TAILS; 'but' and 'are' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: An inelastic material does not stretch, so it is stiff and unyielding.

clue.text: The sensible go after somewhere to live which is on the level

indicators.note: the sensible piece follows the home piece

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, somewhere to live
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Sensible people look for a home that is honest and fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatwise means lying with the flat side down, that is horizontal.

clue.text: The stupid person has to be caught within the distance

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'The stupid person has to be caught within the distance': BE + C inside MILE gives MBECILE, and no clue word supplies the leading I; the clue looks misread or cut, and no source found the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: The stupid person has to be caught within the distance

clue.text: Performed so as to possess. in place of sleep

indicators.note: to possess is put in the place of sleep, inside its letters

parts.note: a bed is where one sleeps
to have is to possess

explanation.surface: Someone acted in order to own something, instead of sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like 'instead of', but 'in' is the container and 'place of sleep' is BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or person that behaved well performed or functioned well.

clue.text: Indicate it is not in the river

indicators.note: the word not is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone points out that something is not in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or point to, so indicate is a synonym.

clue.text: Poor cut out to make a geological formation

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of poor cut are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A poor cut produces a rock feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock exposed at the surface, a feature studied by geologists.

clue.text: Jane's partner among the lasses and lads

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Jane's partner among the lasses and lads': no hidden run, anagram or charade among these words gives WILLIE, and the clue looks misread; no source found the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Jane's partner among the lasses and lads

clue.text: Guide for woman in ancient city

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the name of the city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone guides a woman around an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so this person guides them.

clue.text: Man who makes a revolution over nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the revolution sits above the nothing

parts.note: a roll is one complete turn over
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man stages an uprising over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rollo was the Viking founder of Normandy; here the clue just needs a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollo is a male given name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Dirty act left to be composed with three fingers

indicators.note: the letters of dirty act are composed, put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dirty deed left to be written up by someone with three fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be composed' rearranges DIRTY ACT into TRIDACTY, and L for left follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tridactyl describes a hand or foot that has three digits, a zoological term.

clue.text: Three girls for a composer

parts.note: Vi is short for Violet
Val is short for Valerie
Di is short for Diana

explanation.surface: Three young women are given the name of a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: More recent article of the Pope's church

parts.note: later means more recent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newer item about the Pope's own church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is a grammar word here, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: St John Lateran in Rome is the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Escaped looter I disturbed receives signals from outer space

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of escaped looter I are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A looter who got away is upset to be picking up messages from aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical dish of this kind picks up radio waves from distant stars and galaxies.
